items.stem: A pod is scheduled but traffic is sent to it before the app finishes loading, causing errors. Which configuration fixes this?

options.text: Add a readiness probe so the pod receives traffic only when ready
options.rationale: Correct: readiness probes gate Service endpoints until the app can serve.
Liveness restarts unhealthy pods but does not delay traffic during startup.
More replicas still send traffic to pods before they are ready.
Limits are unrelated to startup readiness.

items.explanation: Correct: readiness probes gate Service endpoints until the app can serve.

items.stem: Which TWO practices follow GKE security guidance for workloads that call Google Cloud APIs? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use Workload Identity to map Kubernetes service accounts to Google service accounts
options.rationale: Correct: Workload Identity avoids long-lived keys.

options.text: Apply least-privilege IAM roles to the mapped service account
options.rationale: Correct: scoping the Google service account limits blast radius.

options.text: Copy a service-account JSON key into a Secret and mount it
options.rationale: Long-lived keys are what Workload Identity is meant to eliminate.

options.text: Grant cluster-admin to all application pods

items.explanation: Correct: both keyed options are right; the distractors are wrong for the reasons given.

items.stem: Your team wants managed nodes with minimal node operations and per-pod billing. Which GKE mode best fits?

options.rationale: Correct: Autopilot manages nodes and bills per pod resource request.
Standard requires managing node pools yourself.

options.text: A self-managed Kubernetes cluster on VMs

options.rationale: Cloud Run is not a Kubernetes cluster for this workload model.

items.explanation: Correct: Autopilot manages nodes and bills per pod resource request.
